# Dhaga

> Dhaga is a private, open-source personal CRM for founders and relationship-driven professionals: capture meetings, notes, messages, introductions, voice memos, and cards, remember the context, search the network, and follow up at the right time. Open-core: the whole CRM is AGPL and runs fully self-hosted, with a source-available cloud tier.

Dhaga (धागा — Hindi for "thread") is a private relationship memory for founders and other relationship-driven professionals: investors, recruiters, real-estate and financial advisors, consultants, and community builders. Capture a meeting or introduction, write or paste a note or message, forward a contact card, note, or photo through WhatsApp or Telegram, scan a card, clip a page with the extension, or import an address book — Dhaga extracts the people, companies and facts, files them in a private knowledge graph, and answers questions like "who do I know at a fintech in Bangalore?" in plain language. Every AI-derived fact keeps a receipt back to the note it came from, so you can verify it or delete it.

What separates it from Dex, Monica or a notes app: the whole CRM is AGPL-licensed and self-hostable, every external dependency (LLM, web search, embeddings, vector store, messaging) sits behind a swappable provider gateway so you can point it at a local model or your own API key, enrichment only ever runs when you ask for it, and full export always works. The free tier is a complete CRM at $0 forever with unlimited capture and notes. Pro is $10 month-to-month or $8/month billed $96 yearly; the first 500 founding seats can request a $79 first year. Power is shown as a coming-soon plan at $30 monthly or $24/month billed $288 yearly and cannot yet be purchased. Dhaga Cloud is in early access; request access at https://www.dhaga.app/#request-access.

Sections run in order of what a reader needs first, not by directory. `## Optional` carries its llms.txt meaning — those URLs are secondary and can be skipped when context is tight: SEO/how-to guides, the per-profession landing pages (each restates the same product for a different job), and internal engineering documents that change weekly. Everything outside `## Optional` is inlined in full at https://www.dhaga.app/llms-full.txt.

- [Dhaga vs Dex: Private CRM vs Auto-Sync CRM](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/dhaga-vs-dex): Dex vs Dhaga compared — automatic LinkedIn/email sync vs open-source privacy and a free tier that actually works. Which personal CRM fits?
- [Dhaga vs Louisa AI: Personal vs Enterprise Graph](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/dhaga-vs-louisa): Louisa AI vs Dhaga — enterprise, firm-owned relationship intelligence vs a private personal CRM you own. Different buyers, compared honestly.
- [Dhaga vs Monica: Open-Source Personal CRM Compared](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/dhaga-vs-monica): Monica vs Dhaga — two open-source, self-hostable personal CRMs compared on AI, capture, and features. Which should you self-host?
- [Dhaga vs OpenVC: Warm Intros vs Investor Database](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/dhaga-vs-openvc): OpenVC vs Dhaga — a fundraising investor database vs a private relationship graph you own. Complementary tools for founders raising a round.
- [Dhaga vs YourPond: Which Personal CRM Remembers?](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/dhaga-vs-yourpond): YourPond vs Dhaga — a polished iOS relationship app vs an open-source, AI-native personal CRM you own. Which remembers your network best?
- [Personal CRM vs LinkedIn: Which Keeps Your Network?](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/guides/personal-crm-vs-linkedin): Why LinkedIn forgets your connections, and how a personal CRM keeps every conversation and follow-up.

## Using Dhaga

- [Using Dhaga](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide): A task-oriented tour of the Dhaga app — capture people anywhere, turn notes into a private knowledge graph, and query it in plain language.
- [AI credits](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/ai-credits): The Credits tab in Settings — how many AI credits you have left this month, what each action costs, and exactly where the ones you spent went.
- [Calendar & reminders](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/calendar): See every follow-up and upcoming birthday on a full-screen calendar — drag to reschedule, schedule date-less ones from the tray, and stay nudged by the notification bell and opt-in reminder emails.
- [Capturing people](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/capturing-people): Add a person to your graph from pasted text, a card photo, voice, your webcam, or a file — with a review step that confirms the fields before saving.
- [Companies](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/companies): View, create, rename, delete, and merge the companies in your graph — with duplicate detection — from a dedicated management page.
- [Confirmations](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/confirmations): Review ambiguous AI suggestions and calendar-date choices without letting uncertainty make a silent decision.
- [Enrich from the web](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/enrich-from-web): Search the public web for a person's footprint on demand — always user-triggered, cited on every finding, and saved as a note you can delete.
- [Custom entities](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/entities): Model the non-person things that connect your people — gyms, schools, projects — as custom entity nodes with their own types.
- [Exploring the graph](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/exploring-the-graph): Your whole network on one canvas — find warm-path intros, open a node's edges in a side panel, toggle layers, and zoom or reset the view.
- [Groups & events](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/groups-and-events): Group the people you met at a gathering into an event, add them in a row from the roster, email a digest, and let Dhaga suggest groups it spots.
- [Importing contacts](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/importing-contacts): Bring an existing address book into Dhaga — from a .vcf or CSV file, a one-click Google or Outlook connection, or the contacts already on your phone.
- [Connect an AI assistant (MCP)](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/mcp): Dhaga speaks the Model Context Protocol, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any other MCP client can read your network and write back to it — ten tools, no AI credits for the reading half.
- [Bulk actions & merging](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/merging-and-bulk-actions): Act on many people at once from the People table — merge duplicates into one record, add a company, tag, star, or forget in a batch — and let Dhaga surface likely duplicates for you.
- [Messaging capture (WhatsApp & Telegram)](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/messaging-capture): Forward a contact card, a note, or a photo to Dhaga's WhatsApp or Telegram bot, reply DONE, and Dhaga saves the person into your graph — capture from your phone with nothing to install.
- [Notes & facts](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/notes-and-facts): Add notes to a person by typing, by voice, or by photo; Dhaga extracts structured facts automatically (or add facts and follow-ups by hand — no AI needed), keeps a receipt on each, and cascades deletions.
- [Search & Ask Dhaga](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/search-and-ask): The ⌘K command palette has two tabs — Search to filter by name, fact, or note, and Ask Dhaga to get a reasoned, receipted answer over your own graph.
- [Settings & import](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/settings): The Settings page — profile, appearance, billing, 2FA, calendar, suggestions, card-photo storage, voice teaching, API keys — and importing your contacts from a file, a Google or Outlook connect, or your phone.
- [Share & invite](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/share-and-invite): Wrapped turns your graph into a contact-free share card you can post anywhere; Invite friends gives you and a friend a free month of Pro.
- [Syncing with your phone](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/syncing-your-phone): Keep your phone's address book and Dhaga in step, both ways — with a three-way merge that never silently overwrites, and a hard line that keeps your notes and facts off every device your contacts sync to.
- [Tasks & recurring follow-ups](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/guide/tasks-and-followups): Track work with or without a person, add optional company context, repeat follow-ups on a calendar cadence, and turn clear note dates into calendar items.

## Self-hosting, extending & contributing

- [API reference](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/api): Generated TypeDoc reference for the shared @dhaga/core package — LLM, search and messaging gateway contracts, prompt builders, and types. Excluded from llms-full.txt (~153 generated pages); browse it on the site.
- [Contributing](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/contributing): The distilled version of how this codebase actually gets built — licensing, the branch/PR workflow, the code standards CI enforces, and the architecture principles.
- [Extending Dhaga](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/extending): Every external capability Dhaga uses — the LLM, web search, and vector retrieval — sits behind a provider-agnostic gateway in @dhaga/core. Add your own by implementing an interface and registering it.
- [Add an LLM provider](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/extending/llm-provider): Implement the LLMClient interface and register an LLMProvider so Dhaga routes extraction and reasoning to your model — Ollama, a BYO-key gateway, or any OpenAI-compatible server.
- [Add a search provider](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/extending/search-provider): Implement the SearchClient interface and register a SearchProvider so Dhaga's enrichment and news-watchlist features run against your web search backend — Brave, SerpAPI, or a self-hosted SearXNG.
- [Add a vector store / retrieval provider](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/extending/vector-store): Swap Dhaga's embedding model and vector store independently through the retrieval gateway — any external engine, as long as declared dimensions match.
- [Self-hosting](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/self-hosting): Run the full AGPL core without Dhaga Cloud — what you get, what you don't, and how the hosted-mode switches work.
- [Cost & scaling on AWS](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/self-hosting/cost-scaling-aws): A service-by-service migration map off Supabase + Vercel, a cost model at 1k / 10k / 100k users, and the scaling architecture — built around the one number that moves the bill: model inference.
- [Deploying](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/self-hosting/deploy): The three ways Dhaga deploys — Vercel, a single persistent server, and Docker — plus the Postgres role and pooling rules that matter in hosted mode.
- [Providers](https://www.dhaga.app/docs/self-hosting/providers): Extend Dhaga with your own LLM, web search, embedding model, or vector store — all through provider-agnostic gateways in @dhaga/core.

## Engineering deep dives

- [Engineering](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering): Deep dives on the hardest problems we solved building Dhaga — rendering a 21k-node graph in the browser, keeping an AI product's unit economics alive, isolating tenants on serverless Postgres. Executive summary up top, full engineering detail below.
- [How we build Dhaga with Claude Code](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/building-with-claude-code): A checked-in rulebook the AI must obey, hooks that gate every single edit, and a persistent memory that survives across sessions. Our AI-assisted engineering workflow — the practices that make an agent a reliable contributor instead of a fast intern who forgets everything.
- [The bill is the model, not the servers](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/metering-the-model): In an AI product, infrastructure is a rounding error and inference is the P&L. How we found the real cost driver in Dhaga, and the guardrails that keep a heavy user from costing us $7,200 a month.
- [Rendering a 21,000-node graph in the browser](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/rendering-21k-node-graph): 63,000 edges, 60fps pans, and a laptop with integrated graphics — without a graph database, a server-side render farm, or a spinner that never ends. How Dhaga renders a whole knowledge graph client-side.
- [A schema that heals itself on cold start](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/self-healing-schema): No migration tool, no migration files, and a 15-second sign-in. How a single content hash turned a full schema replay on every serverless cold start into a no-op — while keeping the zero-config, self-healing setup that makes Dhaga trivial to self-host.
- [Isolating tenants on serverless Postgres](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/tenant-isolation-serverless-postgres): Row-level security is easy to turn on and easy to get catastrophically wrong. How a connection pooler almost leaked one customer's data into another's in Dhaga Cloud, and the transaction-scoped design that makes it impossible on either pooling mode.
- [The feature flag that didn't fire](https://www.dhaga.app/blog/engineering/the-feature-flag-that-didnt-fire): Our documented escape hatch for a native dependency didn't work — the app crashed on deploy anyway. A short war story about how `import` runs before your code does, and why a feature flag can't gate a static import.
